source.original_text:
Attributed ASTIS-authored actual Gaussian Gibbs marginal centered compact-gradient-domain Poincare; faithful source coefficient and standing hypotheses retained.
Let E be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert Borel space with canonical volume, including rank zero. Let V:E→ℝ be C2, 0<α≤β, α‖a‖²≤D²V(x)[a,a]≤β‖a‖² for every x,a, η>0 and βη≤1. Define μ=volume.tilted(−V), J=law(X,X+√ηZ) for independent X∼μ,Z∼N(0,I), and ν=J.snd. Then ν is a probability. There exists one densely defined closable real linear gradient G:L²(ν)⇀L²(ν;E), whose graph consists exactly of AE classes (φ,∇φ) for smooth compactly supported φ, and whose closure has closed graph. For every z in domḠ with ∫z dν=0, [α/(1+αη)]‖z‖²≤‖Ḡz‖². The same G is chosen before every such z. No caller normalization, curvature, Poincare, law, domain, convergence or extra moment certificate is assumed. This is the genuine compact-gradient closure formulation of the source marginal PI; equivalence with a separately defined weighted H1 remains open.
Source boundary: PBPS2609.06905v1 Eq2.13 and AppendixD.2 D6/D10 feeding C3; original C2, two Hessian bounds,0<alpha<=beta and capped positive eta remain.
Explicit extension: Finite real Hilbert/Borel including rank0 explicit; exact compact-gradient closure Poincare, not equality to a separately defined weighted H1. Uniform genuine G selected before all centered domain z.
Actual objects: mu=tilt-volume(-V), J=law(X,X+sqrtetaZ), nu=J.snd; G exact smooth compact scalar/vector-L2 graph, actual closure and actual normalized mean.
Consumer: Actual56 SAME-nu Tu/Ku closure pair, derived coefficient alpha/(1+alphaeta) in sourceC3. Focused Test must identify same G by exact graph, combine56 sharp estimate; no caller PI/law/gradient/domain/normalizer/curvature certificate.

{E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ)*‖v‖^2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ)*‖v‖^2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ)*η ≤ 1) :
    let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x)
    let J := (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
      (fun p : E × E => (p.1,p.1+Real.sqrt η • p.2))
    let ν := J.snd
    IsProbabilityMeasure ν ∧
      ∃ G : Lp ℝ 2 ν →ₗ.[ℝ] Lp E 2 ν,
        Dense (G.domain : Set (Lp ℝ 2 ν)) ∧ G.IsClosable ∧ G.closure.IsClosed ∧
        (∀ (u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) (v : Lp E 2 ν), (u,v) ∈ G.graph ↔
          ∃ φ : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ φ ∧ HasCompactSupport φ ∧
            u =ᵐ[ν] φ ∧ v =ᵐ[ν] gradient φ) ∧
        ∀ z : G.closure.domain,
          (∫ x, (z : Lp ℝ 2 ν) x ∂ν) = 0 →
          ((α : ℝ)/(1+(α : ℝ)*η))*‖(z : Lp ℝ 2 ν)‖^2 ≤ ‖G.closure z‖^2
decoder_context: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space with canonical volume, including rank zero. V is C2, alpha,beta nonnegative with alpha>0 and alpha<=beta; the displayed actual global second derivative lies between alpha and beta times squared direction norm. eta>0,beta*eta<=1 retained.

Measure.tilted is normalized exponential tilting. mu is exactly volume.tilted(-V); J is independent mu times standardGaussian pushforward (x,z)->(x,x+sqrteta*z); nu=J.snd. Probability nu is a conclusion, not a supplied normalization or moment certificate.
Lp F2nu consists of AE classes of strongly measurable square-integrable functions, with canonical strongly measurable representatives. Finite dimension of E does not make L2nu finite dimensional.

G is a genuine partially defined real linear map from scalar L2nu to vector L2nu. Graph iff is exact: represented AE by the SAME smooth compact phi and its genuine Euclidean gradient. Domain is dense; closability means topological graph closure single-valued, and G.closure is the resulting closed partial linear map.

One G and all its exact graph/density/closure properties are chosen BEFORE every z in G.closure.domain. A z is a scalar AE class with actual closed derivative G.closure z. The integral(z)=0 condition restricts the Poincare conclusion to centered z; it is not an extra input assumption on V,nu or a supplied operator.

The conclusion is [alpha/(1+alpha*eta)]*normz^2 <= norm(G.closure z)^2 for every such centered z. No caller measure/kernel/domain/gradient/curvature/Poincare/convergence certificate, extra moment or compactness of z occurs.
No separately defined weak-H1 equivalence, onto macroscopic range, defect square root/inverse, dynamics, algorithmic mixing, main result or cost is asserted.

/-!
# Actual centered Poincare for the Gaussian Gibbs marginal

PBPS arXiv:2609.06905v1 Eq2.13, D.6/D.10 and C.3. The positive C2
normalized marginal is derived from the actual Gibbs/Gaussian law. Posterior
covariance upper and the existing exact smoothed Hessian upper producer give
alpha/(1+alpha eta) and beta/(1+beta eta); all moment, partition and law
adapters are internal. Existing original-domain Poincare is consumed on one
genuine smooth-compact gradient closure selected before all centered inputs.
Original C2/two Hessian bounds and positive capped eta remain. Finite Hilbert,
Borel and rank0 are explicit extensions. This does not identify full weighted
H1, macro range, Gamma/inverses, dynamics, mixing, main results or query costs.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.GaussianMarginalPoincare
open Set MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory InnerProductSpace
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace ContDiff NNReal Topology
noncomputable section
set_option autoImplicit false
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000

theorem actual_gaussian_marginal_centered_poincare
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {α β : ℝ≥0} {η : ℝ}
    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ)*‖v‖^2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ)*‖v‖^2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ)*η ≤ 1) :
    let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x)
    let J := (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
      (fun p : E × E => (p.1,p.1+Real.sqrt η • p.2))
    let ν := J.snd
    IsProbabilityMeasure ν ∧
      ∃ G : Lp ℝ 2 ν →ₗ.[ℝ] Lp E 2 ν,
        Dense (G.domain : Set (Lp ℝ 2 ν)) ∧ G.IsClosable ∧ G.closure.IsClosed ∧
        (∀ (u : Lp ℝ 2 ν) (v : Lp E 2 ν), (u,v) ∈ G.graph ↔
          ∃ φ : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ φ ∧ HasCompactSupport φ ∧
            u =ᵐ[ν] φ ∧ v =ᵐ[ν] gradient φ) ∧
        ∀ z : G.closure.domain,
          (∫ x, (z : Lp ℝ 2 ν) x ∂ν) = 0 →
          ((α : ℝ)/(1+(α : ℝ)*η))*‖(z : Lp ℝ 2 ν)‖^2 ≤ ‖G.closure z‖^2 := by
  classical
  letI : CompleteSpace E := FiniteDimensional.complete ℝ E
  dsimp only
  let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x)
  let J := (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
    (fun p : E × E => (p.1,p.1+Real.sqrt η • p.2))
  let ν := J.snd
  let C := ((Real.sqrt (2*Real.pi*η))⁻¹)^Module.finrank ℝ E
  let A := fun y : E => C*∫ x, Real.exp (-V x-‖y-x‖^2/(2*η)) ∂(volume : Measure E)
  let Vη := fun y : E => -Real.log (A y)
  let R := fun y : E => μ.tilted (fun x => -‖x-y‖^2/(2*η))
  let U := fun y : E => -Real.log (C*∫ x, Real.exp (-‖y-x‖^2/(2*η)) ∂μ)
  let ZV := ∫ x, Real.exp (-V x) ∂(volume : Measure E)
  obtain ⟨hZ,hμ,_hlaw,hIA,hIntA,hTilt,hA,hC2,hshift⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.SmoothedGibbsPotential.smoothed_gibbs_potential
      hα hV (fun x a => (hH x a).1) hη
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := hμ
  have hpair : Measurable (fun p : E × E => (p.1,p.1+Real.sqrt η • p.2)) := by fun_prop
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure J := Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map hpair.aemeasurable
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure ν := Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map measurable_snd.aemeasurable
  have htilt : ν = (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun y => -Vη y) :=
    (Measure.map_map measurable_snd hpair).trans hTilt
  have hC : 0<C := by dsimp only [C]; positivity
  obtain ⟨hRm,_hD,hDD⟩ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.GaussianConvolutionRegularity.gaussian_convolution_derivatives μ hη hC
  have hi := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.StrongConvexGibbsIntegrability.integrable_exp_neg_of_strongConvexOn
    hα (hV.differentiable (by norm_num))
    (AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.HessianStrongConvexity.strongConvexOn_univ_of_fderiv2_lower hV (fun x a => (hH x a).1))
  have hcov (y : E) : ∀ a : E, covarianceBilin (R y) a a ≤ ‖a‖^2/((α : ℝ)+η⁻¹) := by
    let W := fun x => V x+η⁻¹/2*‖x-y‖^2
    have hW : ContDiff ℝ 2 W := hV.add (contDiff_const.mul ((contDiff_id.sub contDiff_const).norm_sq (𝕜:=ℝ)))
    have hVd : Differentiable ℝ V := hV.differentiable (by norm_num)
    have hVdd : Differentiable ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) := (hV.fderiv_right (m:=1) (by norm_num)).differentiable_one
    have hq (x : E) : HasFDerivAt (fun z => η⁻¹/2*‖z-y‖^2)
        (η⁻¹ • innerSL ℝ (x-y)) x := by
      convert (((hasFDerivAt_id x).sub_const y).norm_sq).const_mul (η⁻¹/2)
        using 1 <;> first | rfl | (ext a; simp;ring)
    have hWfd (x : E) : fderiv ℝ W x = fderiv ℝ V x+η⁻¹ • innerSL ℝ (x-y) :=
      ((hVd x).hasFDerivAt.add (hq x)).fderiv
    let J : E →L[ℝ] (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) :=
      {toFun := fun a => innerSL ℝ a
       map_add' := by intros;ext;simp
       map_smul' := by intros;ext;simp
       cont := (innerSL ℝ (E:=E)).continuous}
    have hWdd (x : E) : HasFDerivAt (fderiv ℝ W)
        (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x+η⁻¹ • J) x := by
      rw [show fderiv ℝ W=(fun z => fderiv ℝ V z+η⁻¹ • innerSL ℝ (z-y)) from funext hWfd]
      convert (hVdd x).hasFDerivAt.add ((J.hasFDerivAt.comp x ((hasFDerivAt_id x).sub_const y)).const_smul η⁻¹) using 1 <;> rfl
    have hb (x a : E) : ((α : ℝ)+η⁻¹)*‖a‖^2 ≤ fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ W) x a a ∧
        fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ W) x a a ≤ ((β : ℝ)+η⁻¹)*‖a‖^2 := by
      rw [(hWdd x).fderiv]
      change ((α : ℝ)+η⁻¹)*‖a‖^2 ≤ fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x a a+η⁻¹*inner ℝ a a ∧
        fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x a a+η⁻¹*inner ℝ a a ≤ ((β : ℝ)+η⁻¹)*‖a‖^2
      rw [real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
      constructor <;> nlinarith [(hH x a).1,(hH x a).2]
    have hm : 0<(α : ℝ)+η⁻¹ := add_pos hα (inv_pos.mpr hη)
    have hmM : (α : ℝ)+η⁻¹≤(β : ℝ)+η⁻¹ := by
      simpa only [add_comm] using (add_le_add_right (show (α : ℝ) ≤ (β : ℝ) from hαβ) η⁻¹)
    have hiW := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.StrongConvexGibbsIntegrability.integrable_exp_neg_of_strongConvexOn
      hm (hW.differentiable (by norm_num))
      (AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.HessianStrongConvexity.strongConvexOn_univ_of_fderiv2_lower hW (fun x a => (hb x a).1))
    have hRW : R y=(volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -W x) := by
      dsimp only [R,μ]
      rw [tilted_tilted hi]
      congr 1
      funext x
      simp only [Pi.add_apply,W]
      field_simp [hη.ne']
      ring
    have hX : MemLp id 2 ((volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -W x)) := hRW ▸ (hRm y).2
    rw [hRW]
    exact AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.GibbsLinearCovarianceUpper.gibbs_linear_covariance_upper
      W hW hiW (integral_exp_pos hiW) ((α : ℝ)+η⁻¹) ((β : ℝ)+η⁻¹) hm hmM
      (fun x a => (hb x a).1) (fun x a => (hb x a).2) hX
  have he : U=(fun y => Vη y+Real.log ZV) := funext hshift
  have hd : fderiv ℝ U=fderiv ℝ Vη := by
    rw [he]
    funext y
    exact fderiv_add_const _
  change ∀ y a b, fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ U) y a b = _ at hDD
  rw [hd] at hDD
  let m := (α : ℝ)/(1+(α : ℝ)*η)
  let M := (β : ℝ)/(1+(β : ℝ)*η)
  have hden : 0<1+(α : ℝ)*η := by positivity
  have hbden : 0<1+(β : ℝ)*η := by positivity
  have hm : 0<m := div_pos hα hden
  have hmM : m≤M := by
    dsimp only [m,M]
    apply (div_le_div_iff₀ hden hbden).2
    nlinarith [show (α : ℝ) ≤ (β : ℝ) from hαβ]
  have hlower (y a : E) : m*‖a‖^2 ≤ fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ Vη) y a a := by
    rw [hDD y a a,real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
    have hp : 0<(α : ℝ)+η⁻¹ := add_pos hα (inv_pos.mpr hη)
    calc
      m*‖a‖^2 = ‖a‖^2/η-(‖a‖^2/((α : ℝ)+η⁻¹))/η^2 := by
        dsimp only [m]
        field_simp [hη.ne',hp.ne',hden.ne']
        ring
      _ ≤ ‖a‖^2/η-covarianceBilin (R y) a a/η^2 :=
        sub_le_sub_left (div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (hcov y a) (sq_nonneg η)) _
  have hupper : ∀ y a : E, fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ Vη) y a a ≤ M*‖a‖^2 :=
    (AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.SmoothedHessianUpper.smoothed_hessian_upper
      (show 0<α from hα) hαβ hV hH hη).2
  have hI : Integrable (fun y => Real.exp (-Vη y)) (volume : Measure E) := by
    have hexp (y : E) : Real.exp (-Vη y)=A y := by
      dsimp only [Vη];rw [neg_neg,Real.exp_log (hA y)]
    simpa only [hexp] using hIA
  have hZη : 0<∫ y, Real.exp (-Vη y) ∂(volume : Measure E) := integral_exp_pos hI
  obtain ⟨G,hDense,hClose,hClosed,hGraph⟩ :=
    GaussianMarginalGradient.gaussian_marginal_gradient_closable μ hη
  refine ⟨inferInstance,G,hDense,hClose,hClosed,hGraph,?_⟩
  have hPI : ∀ (D : Lp ℝ 2 ν →ₗ.[ℝ] Lp E 2 ν), D.IsClosable →
      (∀ (a : Lp ℝ 2 ν) (F : Lp E 2 ν), (a,F) ∈ D.graph ↔
        ∃ φ : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ φ ∧ HasCompactSupport φ ∧
          a =ᵐ[ν] φ ∧ F =ᵐ[ν] gradient φ) →
      ∀ z : D.closure.domain, (∫ x, (z : Lp ℝ 2 ν) x ∂ν)=0 →
        m*‖(z : Lp ℝ 2 ν)‖^2 ≤ ‖D.closure z‖^2 := by
    rw [htilt]
    exact CenteredDomainPoincare.gibbs_centered_domain_poincare
      Vη hC2 hI hZη m M hm hmM hlower hupper
  exact hPI G hClose hGraph

end
end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.GaussianMarginalPoincare

steps.title: Derive the actual marginal law and its potential
steps.text: Original lower curvature and C2 yield positive finite ZV and probability μ. The existing smoothed Gibbs producer gives Aη(y)=cη∫exp(−V(x)−‖y−x‖²/(2η))dx, positive C2 Vη=−logAη, ∫Aη=ZV and the exact actual add-noise law ν=volume.tilted(−Vη). The normalized negative-log density Uη differs from Vη by logZV; no normalizer or law equality is supplied.
steps.lean: SmoothedGibbsPotential.smoothed_gibbs_potential; htilt; hIA; hIntA; hA; hC2; hshift; Measure.map_map

steps.title: Produce the true conditional covariance bound
steps.text: The actual Gaussian derivative producer supplies probability and vectorL2 moments of R_y=μ.tilted(x↦−‖x−y‖²/(2η)). Derive R_y=volume.tilted(−W_y) with W_y(x)=V(x)+‖x−y‖²/(2η). Its genuine Hessian lies between α+η⁻¹ and β+η⁻¹. Strong convexity gives exp-L1 and a positive partition internally. Existing original-domain covariance upper applies to the actual posterior and its produced moments; no covariance or moment certificate is a theorem premise.
steps.lean: GaussianConvolutionRegularity.gaussian_convolution_derivatives; hRm; hcov; hWdd; hb; hiW; hRW; GibbsLinearCovarianceUpper.gibbs_linear_covariance_upper

steps.title: Obtain both exact marginal curvature constants
steps.text: The actual normalized Hessian identity and additive partition shift imply D²Vη(y)[a,a]=‖a‖²/η−CovR_y(a,a)/η². The produced covariance upper gives mη=α/(1+αη). Reuse the already verified generic SmoothedHessianUpper producer for Mη=β/(1+βη); it retains the true Cramer-Rao/posterior inputs and is not replaced by a coarse certificate. α≤β gives mη≤Mη.
steps.formula: D^2V_\eta(y)[a,a]=\frac{\|a\|^2}{\eta}-\frac{\operatorname{Cov}_{R_y}(a,a)}{\eta^2},\quad0<m_\eta=\frac\alpha{1+\alpha\eta}\le M_\eta=\frac\beta{1+\beta\eta},\quad m_\eta I\preceq D^2V_\eta\preceq M_\eta I.
steps.lean: hDD; he; hd; hlower; SmoothedHessianUpper.smoothed_hessian_upper; hupper; hm; hmM

lesson.lean_statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert Borel space with canonical volume, including rank zero. Let V:E→ℝ be C2, 0<α≤β, α‖a‖²≤D²V(x)[a,a]≤β‖a‖² for every x,a, η>0 and βη≤1. Define μ=volume.tilted(−V), J=law(X,X+√ηZ) for independent X∼μ,Z∼N(0,I), and ν=J.snd. Then ν is a probability. There exists one densely defined closable real linear gradient G:L²(ν)⇀L²(ν;E), whose graph consists exactly of AE classes (φ,∇φ) for smooth compactly supported φ, and whose closure has closed graph. For every z in domḠ with ∫z dν=0, [α/(1+αη)]‖z‖²≤‖Ḡz‖². The same G is chosen before every such z. No caller normalization, curvature, Poincare, law, domain, convergence or extra moment certificate is assumed. This is the genuine compact-gradient closure formulation of the source marginal PI; equivalence with a separately defined weighted H1 remains open.

decoder.reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space equipped with its Borel measurable structure and canonical volume measure. The zero-dimensional case is included. Let V : E -> R be twice continuously differentiable. Let alpha and beta be nonnegative real numbers with alpha > 0 and alpha <= beta, and let eta be real with eta > 0 and beta eta <= 1. Assume, for every x,v in E, that
alpha ||v||^2 <= (D(DV)(x)[v])[v] <= beta ||v||^2.
Here D(DV)(x)[v] is the derivative of the derivative of V at x applied to v, and its value is then applied to v again.
Define mu = volume.tilted(x -> -V(x)), using normalized exponential tilting. Thus the measure is the normalized exponential tilt of canonical volume by exp(-V); this is the actual named measure construction, with its normalization built into tilted. Define J to be the pushforward of mu tensor stdGaussian(E) under (x,w) -> (x, x + sqrt(eta) w), and define nu to be the second marginal of J. The standard Gaussian is on E and is independent of the mu coordinate in this product construction.
Then nu is a probability measure, and there exists one partially defined real linear operator G from L^2(nu; R) to L^2(nu; E) with all the following properties. Its domain is dense in L^2(nu; R). It is closable, and its graph-closure operator Gbar is closed. For every u in L^2(nu; R) and v in L^2(nu; E), (u,v) is in the graph of G if and only if there exists a single infinitely continuously differentiable compactly supported function phi : E -> R such that u = phi nu-almost everywhere and v = grad(phi) nu-almost everywhere, using the genuine Euclidean gradient of that same phi.
For this same G, for every z in the domain of Gbar, if integral z dnu = 0, then
[alpha / (1 + alpha eta)] ||z||_{L^2(nu; R)}^2 <= ||Gbar z||_{L^2(nu; E)}^2.
Elements of these L^2 spaces are almost-everywhere classes of strongly measurable square-integrable functions; the displayed integral uses the canonical representative of the scalar class. Gbar z is the actual closed derivative determined by the closure of the exact graph just specified. The density, closability, closedness and exact graph properties belong to the single existentially chosen operator before the universal quantification over centered z. No measure, kernel, domain, gradient operator, curvature certificate, Poincare certificate, moment certificate, or convergence certificate is provided as an additional hypothesis. The statement does not assert an independently defined weak-H^1 identification, surjectivity, inverse or square-root operators, dynamics, algorithmic mixing, a broader result, or a cost estimate.

objects.E: Finite-dimensional real normed additive commutative group with real inner-product-space structure, a measurable structure equal to its Borel structure, and canonical volume; rank zero is allowed.
objects.alpha_beta: Elements of R>=0, coerced to R in the displayed Hessian and conclusion coefficients.
objects.G: An existentially chosen partially defined real linear map Lp R 2 nu -> Lp E 2 nu.
objects.Gbar: G.closure, the closed partial real linear operator defined by topological graph closure of the closable G.

domains.scalar_L2: AE classes of strongly measurable square-integrable E -> R functions, with canonical representatives.
domains.vector_L2: AE classes of strongly measurable square-integrable E -> E functions, with canonical representatives.
domains.G_domain: Exactly scalar classes admitting a smooth compactly supported representative phi, whose graph value is represented by grad(phi). Domain density is a conclusion.
domains.Gbar_domain: The domain of the actual closure of G; the statement supplies no separate identification with a weak-H1 space.
domains.z: A subtype element of Gbar.domain, coerced to scalar L2 in its mean and norm.

quantifiers: Universally quantify the ambient type E and the stated typeclass structures, V, alpha, beta, eta, and proofs of all displayed assumptions.
The Hessian bounds hold for every x and every direction v in E.
After the exact let-bound definitions of mu, J, nu, conclude probability of nu and existence of one G.
For that G, density, closability, closure closedness, and the exact graph iff all hold.
The exact graph iff quantifies every scalar L2 class u and vector L2 class v; phi is existential inside this iff and is shared by both AE equalities.
Only after choosing the same G and all its properties, quantify every z in G.closure.domain, with mean zero as the antecedent of the inequality.
assumptions: E : Type*, NormedAddCommGroup E, InnerProductSpace R E, FiniteDimensional R E, MeasurableSpace E, BorelSpace E.
V : E -> R and ContDiff R 2 V.
For all x,v : E, (alpha : R)*||v||^2 <= (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x v) v and (fderiv R (fderiv R V) x v) v <= (beta : R)*||v||^2.

conclusion.operator: Existence of a single genuine partially defined real linear G with Dense G.domain, G.IsClosable and G.closure.IsClosed.
conclusion.exact_graph: For every u,v, (u,v) in G.graph iff there is phi : E -> R with ContDiff R infinity phi, HasCompactSupport phi, u = phi AE[nu] and v = gradient phi AE[nu].
conclusion.centered_closed_domain_bound: For every z : G.closure.domain, integral z dnu = 0 implies ((alpha : R)/(1+(alpha : R)*eta))*||z||^2 <= ||G.closure z||^2.

scopes.law: Specific normalized tilted-volume plus independent standard-Gaussian pushforward and second marginal; no arbitrary supplied measure or kernel.
scopes.uniformity: One G serves all centered z in its closure domain; no operator may be selected anew for each z.
scopes.mean_condition: An antecedent on each z, not an added assumption on V, nu, or a supplied operator.
scopes.boundary: The assertion ends at the probability/exact closable gradient graph/Poincare inequality. No weak-H1 equivalence, surjectivity, defect inverse or square root, dynamics, mixing, broader theorem or query cost is asserted.

constant_dependencies.coefficient: alpha/(1+alpha*eta), with alpha coerced from R>=0 to R.
constant_dependencies.beta: Appears in assumptions including beta*eta <= 1; absent from the displayed conclusion coefficient.
constant_dependencies.other: No unnamed constant; the displayed coefficient has no explicit dimension, V, or z dependence.
